correctness.rationale: Integrating the order-one Cauchy kernel gives the signed simple-pole endpoint sum. With the common denominator, the numerator has degree exactly 2n−2 and is nonzero at all endpoints, so n−1 upper-half-plane zeros counted with multiplicity is equivalent to no real zeros. Outside the pulses every summand is positive. In pulse k the sign is the sign of Φ_k−w_k, with strictly negative limiting sign at each interior endpoint. This gives necessity including equality and sufficiency of the strict maximum inequalities. They are homogeneous linear tests indexed by compact real intervals; the maxima are continuous functions of w. For equal positive heights, the contribution from the other pulses is strictly smaller than the integral of the positive kernel over the entire complement of pulse k. That latter integral equals the absolute value of the negative own-pulse summand, independently confirming strict feasibility. Mixing any positive weakly feasible vector with the equal-height vector shows that the positive-relative boundary consists exactly of weakly feasible vectors with at least one tight inequality; at the interior maximizer both F and its real derivative vanish. This is not a converse for arbitrary multiple real roots. For two pulses, computing the quadratic's discriminant gives the stated strict gap test and its double and distinct real regimes. As an exact threshold check, intervals [−1,0], [1/4,5/4] with weights (4,1) give P(z)=5(z−1/2)^2. The one-pulse case has no zeros and no boundary inside the positive orthant.
residual_risks: The boundary statement is relative to strictly positive amplitudes; zero weights can cause pole cancellation.

evidence: F is the ordinary Cauchy transform of the signed endpoint measure with residues −w_j at a_j and +w_j at b_j. For equal weights it is a constant times −R′/R, where R is a real rational interlacing product; integer weights similarly give a rational product with multiplicities. General positive real amplitudes need not give a rational product.

The exact chamber is the preimage of strict positivity on the real line under the linear map w↦P_w. The inspected discrete-transform localization theorem is about function spaces, not this specific coefficient domain.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The signed-measure and polynomial formulations explain why generic zero localization, rational critical-point bounds and positive-polynomial convexity are relevant. None of the inspected statements supplies the pulse sign constraints, a strict witness for all interval geometries and the sharp contrast test together.

originality.rationale: Credit the pulse-specific, all-positive-amplitude chamber, a strictly feasible equal-height ray for every separated geometry, and the sharp width–gap–contrast calculation together. The conjugate-pair count, convexity of the positive-polynomial preimage and equal-height rational interlacing are classical mechanisms, not separate originality claims. The inspected wavelet and Cauchy-transform papers do not give the full chamber or an immediately applicable classification of the paired, alternating-residue family.
residual_risks: An older paired-endpoint or alternating-residue theorem could be equivalent; in particular Walsh original full text remained unavailable.
Bounded catalogue and literature searches do not establish universal priority.

value.rationale: This gives a usable complete criterion in the original pulse amplitudes for the maximal upper-half-plane zero census, not just a generic root bound. The nonempty convex geometry gives feasible interpolations between designs; the boundary and explicit two-pulse formula identify when amplitude contrast defeats zero retention. These facts are useful in the holomorphic signal model without needing a larger wavelet theorem.
residual_risks: No noise robustness, overlapping-pulse criterion, or generic simplicity claim follows. For general n, checking chamber membership still requires one-variable maxima.
